gap: No result ChatGPT got states that a 16-inch MacBook Pro only takes the full 140 W through Apple's USB-C to MagSafe 3 cable, or through Apple's 240 W USB-C cable on the Nov 2023 and later models. ChargerLab measured that an M1 Max 16-inch on a 140 W power bank drew about 130 W through MagSafe but dropped to 90 W on a USB-C to USB-C cable.
standout_why: Compared against Macworld (cited) and rottenwifi.com '15 Best Laptop Power Banks' (rank 4). The cited Wirecutter page could not be read: the proxy URL now returns only a block message, and nytimes.com refused the fetch. Macworld only says the 16-inch Pro 'can be fast-charged at 140W' and should use a 'PD 3.1 power bank'. It mentions 'Apple's USB-C to MagSafe 3 Cable or the included 240W USB-C cable' in passing in its Anker Prime 26K entry, but never says that a plain USB-C cable limits older 16-inch models. Rottenwifi covers the generic part: '140W is worthwhile only when the laptop supports USB PD 3.1… and the cable supports the required 5A extended-power mode'. It does not name the MagSafe 3 requirement, the Nov 2023 model cutoff for USB-C, or any measured drop. No rival gives Apple's own list of combinations or a measured 130 W vs 90 W.
decides: This confirms the 140 W picks (UGREEN 145W, Anker Prime 26K A110A) only for 16-inch MacBook Pro owners who also use a USB-C to MagSafe 3 cable, or Apple's 240 W USB-C cable on a Nov 2023 or later 16-inch. With an ordinary USB-C to USB-C cable, a 2021 16-inch gets about 90 W in testing. In that case a 100 W bank like the Anker A1695 or the Baseus FC41's 100 W port performs about the same, for less money and weight. Every 14-inch Pro and every Air fast-charges over any USB-C charge cable at 96 W or more, so 140 W adds nothing for them.

findings.label: Supported 140 W fast-charge setups, in Apple's words
findings.value: "140W USB-C Power Adapter + USB-C to MagSafe 3 Cable"; "140W USB-C Power Adapter + 240W USB-C Charge Cable for MacBook Pro (16-inch, Nov 2023) or later"
findings.source_title: Fast charge your MacBook Air or MacBook Pro - Apple Support
findings.note: For the 16-inch, Apple lists no plain USB-C charge cable. The only USB-C option is its 240 W cable, and only on Nov 2023 or later models. The 14-inch Pro and the Air do list 'USB-C to MagSafe 3 Cable or USB-C charge cable' with 96 W and 140 W adapters (the Air also with 70 W, and 67 W on the 13.6-inch).

findings.product: general (Apple MacBook Pro 14-inch and MacBook Air)
findings.label: Lowest Apple adapter listed for fast charging, and the cable allowed
findings.value: 14-inch Pro: 96 W adapter with 'USB-C to MagSafe 3 Cable or USB-C charge cable'; Air: 70 W (67 W on the 13.6-inch) with the same cables
findings.source_title: Fast charge your MacBook Air or MacBook Pro - Apple Support
findings.note: Apple's adapter combinations translated to a power bank: a 100 W USB-C port covers fast charging on the 14-inch Pro and the Air; 140 W is never required for them.

findings.product: general (MacBook Pro 16-inch M1 Max on a 140 W power bank)
findings.label: Measured charging power by cable
findings.value: about 130 W through a USB-C to MagSafe 3 cable (27 V mode); 90 W through a USB-C to USB-C cable
findings.source_title: ChargerLab review of Baseus 140W power bank (PPADM140, 24,000 mAh / 86.4 Wh), 2023-10-26
findings.note: ChargerLab test on the USB-C1 port: 'the power can be up to 130W' with MagSafe 3; with C-to-C 'the power naturally dropped to 90W'. The test is on a Baseus bank, not one of our candidates. It shows the laptop-side limit.

findings.label: Voltage needed for 140 W, and the old ceiling
findings.value: 140 W needs the 28 V fixed level; before PD 3.1, USB PD topped out at 100 W (20 V × 5 A cable)
findings.note: USB-IF: 'New 28V, 36V, and 48V fixed voltages enable up to 140W, 180W and 240W power levels' and 'Prior to this update, USB PD was limited to 100W using a solution based on 20V using USB Type-C cables rated at 5A.' The new levels need cables that meet the 240 W requirements in USB Type-C Release 2.1.

findings.label: Cable condition stated by the maker (input side)
findings.value: 140 W input needs a 140 W charger and a 5 A cable; 250 W input needs both USB-C ports, each with a 5 A cable and a 140 W charger
findings.note: Footnote quoted: 'Achieve 140W input with a compatible 140W charger and a 5A cable.' Page price $229.99. The page does not list box contents. Macworld says the bank includes a 240 W USB-C cable.

findings.label: Port that delivers 140 W, and cable
findings.value: 1× USB-C at 140 W PD 3.1, 1× USB-C at 100 W PD 3.0, 1× USB-A at 22.5 W; 145 W total; no built-in cable
findings.source_title: Best laptop power banks for Apple MacBook 2026 | Macworld
findings.note: From Macworld's spec list and cons ('No built-in cable'). A 16-inch Pro reaches 140 W only from USB-C1, and only with a MagSafe 3 cable or Apple's 240 W cable (Nov 2023 or later model).
